import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle the 'Sleep Disorder' column: replace NaN with 'No Disorder'
# This ensures all data points are categorized and included in the plot.
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a clean and professional style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create an insightful scatter plot to visualize the relationship between
# Sleep Duration and Age, while also showing the impact of Sleep Disorders (color)
# and Stress Level (point size).
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Age',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',  # Color points by Sleep Disorder category
    size='Stress Level',   # Size points by Stress Level (ordinal, higher stress = larger point)
    sizes=(50, 600),       # Define the range of point sizes for better visual distinction
    alpha=0.7,             # Set transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    palette='tab10',       # Use a qualitative color palette suitable for categorical data
    linewidth=0            # Remove linewidth for cleaner points
)

# Add a descriptive title and axis labels
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Age: Impact of Sleep Disorders and Stress Level', fontsize=16, pad=15)
plt.xlabel('Age (Years)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Sleep Duration (Hours)', fontsize=12)

# Position the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with data points
# Seaborn automatically generates appropriate titles for the hue and size legends.
plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Enhance readability with grid lines
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure as a high-resolution PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

)

plt.ylabel('Sleep Duration (Hours)', fontsize=12)
